title: Pro bono Work to Empower and Represent Act of 2018
official_summary:
Pro bono Work to Empower and Represent Act of 2018 or the POWER Act

(Sec. 3) This bill requires the chief judge for each judicial district to conduct public events to promote pro bono legal services for survivors of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking.

Additionally, the chief judge for a judicial district that contains an Indian tribe or tribal organization must conduct, at least once during each two-year period, a public event to promote pro bono legal services for Indian or Alaska Native victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking.

A chief judge must, in conducting public events, seek to maximize the local impact and the provision of high-quality pro bono legal services to survivors.

(Sec. 4) Chief judges must report to the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts on the public events they conduct. The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts must compile and summarize the reports and submit them to Congress.

summary.headline: This law requires federal court chief judges to hold public events that encourage free legal help for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and stalking.
summary.what_it_does: Each federal judicial district's chief judge must hold public events promoting pro bono (free) legal services for survivors of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking. A district that includes an Indian tribe or tribal organization must hold at least one such event every two years aimed at Indian and Alaska Native victims. Chief judges must report on these events to the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, which compiles the reports and sends them to Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Survivors of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking
who_it_affects.how: They may have more access to free legal help because federal courts are required to promote these services through public events.

who_it_affects.how: Districts with tribes must hold a promotional event at least once every two years focused on free legal services for them.

who_it_affects.how: Each chief judge must organize public events and report on them to the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts.

who_it_affects.group: Lawyers who do pro bono work
